title: PinnacleGrid runtime escape plan and parity probe
summary: Initial discovery for PinnacleGrid's escape plan off their current managed LLM vendor. Discussed parity testing approach, constraints around private deployments (VPC/KMS/HSM), and quick pilot options on Redwood Dedicated. Agreed next steps: share security pack, run a 2-week parity pilot, and schedule infra deep-dive with their infra team.
action_items: Connor Patel - Produce proposed benchmark script (latency/throughput/token-profile) - 2028-10-17
Maya Chen - Send pricing options for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (3 options) - 2028-10-15
PinnacleGrid/Diego Ramos - Share current prompt set + perf traces (95th/median latency) - 2028-10-14
Priya Singh - Provide list of compliance questions and residency constraints - 2028-10-16
next_steps: Redwood to send security packet link and sample SLA
Kickoff 2-week parity pilot on Dedicated (small reserved pool)
Schedule technical deep dive (vLLM/TGI mapping) with Pinnacle infra and runtime owners
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-10-12
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 54 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Connor Patel (Redwood SE), Alice Navarro (CTO, PinnacleGrid), Diego Ramos (ML Eng, PinnacleGrid), Priya Singh (Head Security, PinnacleGrid)

Auto-summary (auto): PinnacleGrid is planning to exit current managed provider and wants to understand Redwood options for parity, private deployment needs (KMS/HSM), quantization/compatibility with their vLLM stack, and cost/latency tradeoffs. They want a short pilot to validate parity and perf.

[00:00:08] Maya Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining, I think we have about 55 min today, so we'll go through goals. quick intro, I'm Maya, AE on the inference team at Redwood. Connor is our SE who will lead the technical bits.
[00:00:20] Alice Navarro: Hi, Alice here. thanks. We're trying to do a vendor escape plan, timeline is Q4 to have a fallback and Q1 to start traffic. We currently are heavily on a managed provider but run a custom vLLM service in-house for some s3-sent prep, and we need an exit path that preserves our eval parity.
[00:00:42] Connor Patel: Great, thanks Alice. can you say which managed provider? I know you can share high level.
[00:00:47] Diego Ramos: We're on a mix — primary workload on OpenAI-ish hosted endpoints, plus an internal v LLM cluster (vLLM/TGI stack) for cheaper local inference. We also run some fine-tuned variants and have a prefix KV cache approach.
[00:01:08] Priya Singh: From security standpoint we need SOC2 certs, SAML SSO, KMS/HSM integrations and proof of data residency for EU traffic. Also audit logs accessible for 90 days initially.
[00:01:23] Maya Chen: Understood. that's a pretty common combo. Redwood supports Hosted (fast onboarding), Dedicated reserved pools, and Private (VPC / on-prem). We can integrate customer KMS and support HSM via our private plane, and we have audit logs in the Console. I'll drop the security pack after the call.
[00:01:40] Alice Navarro: What about parity testing — we have an in-house eval harness. we need to be sure outputs match within tolerance and that latency/quality regressions are measurable.
[00:01:52] Connor Patel: Good question. Our approach is to run your prompt set through both the current provider and Redwood candidate models (including quantized variants) and compare rouge/bleu/LLM-eval metrics plus human review where needed. we'd also capture token-level cost and 95th percentile latency across identical sequence distributions. For vLLM compatibility, we'll map the KV cache semantics — sometimes the saved ability to resume atten- uh saved KV state is implemented differently, so we'll run an interoperability test harness.
[00:02:30] Diego Ramos: That KV cache thing has bitten us before, if the runtime prunes or reorders the cache we see different outputs. also our fine-tuned head uses position ids pretty aggressively.
[00:02:45] Connor Patel: Absolutely, so we'll include structural tests: identical kv warm / cache hits, cache miss behavior, and step-by-step generation traces. we also test with same tokenizer and tokenization offsets.
[00:02:58] Maya Chen: quick clarifying, when you say "fine-tuned head" is it just a linear head or do you run LoRA adapters?
[00:03:05] Diego Ramos: Mostly LoRA adapters, plus a small adapter chain for safety filtering.
[00:03:11] Priya Singh: On security items, can Redwood support customer-managed keys? that's a hard requirement.
[00:03:18] Connor Patel: Yes, customer-managed KMS is supported for Private deploys. For Hosted we offer envelope encryption with Redwood-managed keys or enterprise customers can bring keys in Dedicated via a VPC connector. HSM can be provisioned in Private. I'll put the specifics in the security doc link.
[00:03:36] Alice Navarro: Great. how do you approach canary or rollout? we need gradual cutover and a fallback to the old provider quickly.
[00:03:44] Maya Chen: You can do traffic-splitting via our Console with per-route model pins and automatic fallback rules. For big regressions we support instant rollback to a pinned provider. For Dedicated we can proxy to their endpoints or our hosted fallback for burst capacity.
[00:03:59] Diego Ramos: Cost is also a factor — our infra team keeps pushing to minimize tokens/kg cost. any tips?
[00:04:07] Connor Patel: Yes, Redwood Optimize gives recommendations: batching windows, KV caching, quantization profiles per model. For example, switching to 4-bit quantized model for internal low-risk workloads can cut token cost ~2.5x with small latency change. We'll show corollary numbers in the benchmark script.
[00:04:26] Alice Navarro: On quantization, are you compatible with the quantization knobs we use with vllm/TGI? sometimes the quantized kernels behave differently.
[00:04:34] Connor Patel: We maintain model variant compatibility matrices — some 4-bit profiles are architecture dependent. We'll run the same quantization toolchain you use if you can share it, else we replicate it and compare outputs. noted as part of the parity checklist.
[00:04:49] Priya Singh: Do you have SOC2 type II? and what's retention for audit logs?
[00:04:55] Maya Chen: Yes we are SOC2 Type II. audit logs retention configurable; enterprise packages support 13 months, default is 90 days. We'll include a SOC2 summary and example audit export in the packet.
[00:05:10] Alice Navarro: Nice. what's the suggested pilot shape? we want minimal risk but representative workload.
[00:05:16] Connor Patel: A typical pilot: 2 weeks, Dedicated reserved pool with 2-4 GPUs matching your seq/throughput (we'll size after we see traces). Run the parity harness and the regression tests. We instrument with A/B traffic and tracing via Console so you can compare token costs, latency percentiles, and output diffs.
[00:05:31] Diego Ramos: That sounds reasonable. who will run benchmarks? we'll need someone from Redwood to provide the harness and we'll run it in our environment?
[00:05:39] Connor Patel: We can run both ways. Option A: you provide traces and we run the harness against our Dedicated instance. Option B: we give you a containerized harness to run in your infra against your vLLM/TGI cluster. Most teams do option A for speed.
[00:05:55] Alice Navarro: For the rollout timeline — if pilot is in mid-Oct, what's realistic for production cutover?
[00:06:02] Maya Chen: If pilot shows parity and no critical regressions, some customers have a phased cutover in 4-8 weeks. SLA and contract work can add time. We'll outline a recommended timeline after the pilot.
[00:06:15] Priya Singh: We have EU data residency constraints — can the Dedicated pool be region pinned?
[00:06:21] Connor Patel: Yes, Dedicated capacity can be region restricted and we support dedicated VPC endpoints for traffic. Private deployments give you full on-prem control if you need absolute residency.
[00:06:33] Diego Ramos: A technical thing: our prompt engineering depends on deterministic sampling in some cases. does Redwood expose sampler seeding?
[00:06:41] Connor Patel: We do expose seed control and deterministic sampling options in the API, but some quantized kernels may affect floating point determinism — we'll include determinism checks in the parity scripts.
[00:06:55] Alice Navarro: How do you handle model upgrades and version pinning?
[00:07:01] Maya Chen: You can pin model versions per route and do canary rollouts. There's also automatic fallback to a pinned older variant if latency or error thresholds exceed SLOs.
[00:07:12] Diego Ramos: Any gotchas when mapping from OpenAI-style endpoints to Redwood? we use a lot of function-calling behaviors and structured outputs.
[00:07:20] Connor Patel: We support function/tool calling and structured outputs; sometimes schemas differ. We'll map your call patterns and ensure the model variants preserve function-call tokens and structure. Also note that our streaming semantics might chunk differently which can affect some realtime clients; we'll test streaming parity.
[00:07:42] Maya Chen: quick note on pricing: we'll send three configurations — Hosted pay-as-you-go, Dedicated reserved (monthly), and Private (license + infra). We'll include estimated token cost delta based on your current usage.
[00:07:55] Priya Singh: For compliance, we need a list of sub processors and a data flow diagram.
[00:08:01] Maya Chen: We'll include a subprocessor list and a high-level data flow diagram in the security pack.
[00:08:10] Alice Navarro: ok, let's talk about the vLLM/TGI mapping — Diego you mentioned you run TGI on some clusters, what exactly is custom?
[00:08:19] Diego Ramos: We use TGI + vLLM wrappers for token streaming and a custom prompt cache layer. We also push some pre-tokenized chunks and sometimes rely on half-precision fp16 kernels.
[00:08:31] Connor Patel: We'll need your model artifacts and a few sample weights if possible. For packaging we accept standard formats but some converters are needed for LoRA stacks. We'll list conversion steps in the tech brief.
[00:08:44] Alice Navarro: Is there a recommended conversion path for LoRA + position id tweaks? last migration we had to rebase positions which changed outputs.
[00:08:51] Connor Patel: We have a conversion cookbook — position id rebasing is a known edge case. We'll run a spot check and include a script that replays tokens to verify identical position behavior.
[00:09:05] Maya Chen: Alright, any blocker from your side to start a pilot?
[00:09:09] Diego Ramos: We need to confirm costs to finance and get security sign-off. Also need an infra deep-dive so we can size vCPU/gpu and network.
[00:09:21] Priya Singh: Security wants to see the SOC2 report and KMS integration docs before we sign any contract.
[00:09:29] Maya Chen: We'll send the SOC2 summary and a KMS integration guide after this call. Also we'll propose dates for the pilot start.
[00:09:36] Alice Navarro: Great. would you also be able to run an initial smoke test with 1k requests to validate basic parity?
[00:09:42] Connor Patel: Yes we can run a smoke test as soon as we have the prompt set. Ideally we mirror the 1k with same token distribution.
[00:09:50] Maya Chen: I'll follow up with a calendar invite for a technical deep dive and the security packet link: https://redwood.example.com/security/pinnaclegrid-packet (placeholder).
[00:10:01] Diego Ramos: cool, can you also include a sample benchmark spreadsheet format so we can compare columns?
[00:10:07] Connor Patel: Yes — we'll attach a template with columns for prompt id, input tokens, output tokens, median latency, p95 latency, token-cost, quality-metric, diff-score.
[00:10:20] Alice Navarro: timing wise we need to move quickly, finance wants numbers by next week.
[00:10:25] Maya Chen: We'll aim to send pricing and the packet by 2028-10-15.
[00:10:31] Priya Singh: One more question — data deletion guarantees? we have contractual requirements to delete user data on request.
[00:10:38] Connor Patel: We support data deletion and can provide proofs of deletion for customer-owned data in Private and Dedicated. For Hosted there are standard retention windows but enterprise controls allow for stricter policies. We'll include deletion SLA options in the contract appendix.
[00:10:54] Alice Navarro: Ok that's everything I had for high level. any final notes?
[00:10:59] Maya Chen: To recap — Redwood to send security pack and SOC2, pricing options, benchmark template; Connor to produce the benchmark script and we'll schedule the tech deep-dive. Pinnacle to share prompt set and perf traces.
[00:11:14] Diego Ramos: sounds good. thanks everyone.

(Transcript continues with short clarifying Q&A and brief mention of logistics; noises, small interruptions, and an instance where speaker labels got swapped briefly)

[00:29:02] Alice Navarro: sorry quick clarifying, what did you mean by automatic fallback for Dedicated?
[00:29:07] Connor Patel: meaning we can proxy to hosted fallback endpoints or route to another model variant instantly by policy. it's configurable per route.

[00:38:40] Priya Singh: We'll need a contact for security reviews — can it be you Maya?
[00:38:45] Maya Chen: yes I'll be primary but I'll loop in our security PM as well. contact email: maya.chen@redwood.example.com (placeholder).

[00:48:55] Maya Chen: ok thanks everyone, we'll follow up.
[00:54:00] Maya Chen: meeting end.
